To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

supplementation of lutein (and zeaxanthin) in the diet of hihi (Notiomyystis cinctia) led to increased concentration in egg yolks, nestlings and plasma and also led to increased retinol and decreased alpha tocopherol concentration in the plasma of nestlings, and increased concentration of selenium in egg yolk.
the carotenoids lutein and zexanthin, and vitamin E are utilised by hihis and that supplementation of lutein, zeaxanthin and selenium increases their concentration in egg yolks and plasma.

lutein and zeaaxanthin were the carotenoids used by hihi, that selenium was present at unexpectedly high concentrations and that supplementation of lutein or zeaxanthin increased the concentration of selenium in the egg yolk and retinol in nestling plasma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integrated antioxidant system in a free-living and endangered passerine, and the modulatory effects of carotenoid dietary supplementation.
the antioxidant system of an endangered passerine bird and its interaction with dietary carotenoids.
the identification of numerous components of the integrated antioxidant system in a free-living endangered passerine bird.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the integrated antioxidant system is complex and dynamic, with interactions between components.
carotenoid supplementation can modulate the antioxidant system of a novel species, the hihi, through a number of different mechanisms.

supplementation with lutein and/or zeaxanthin increased the concentration of these carotenoids in egg yolk and plasma, increased the concentration of retinol and selenium in egg yolk, decreased the concentration of alpha-tocopherols in plasma and decreased the concentration of gamma-tocopherols and alpha-tocopherals in yolk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integrated antioxidant system can be manipulated by carotenoid supplementation in free living animals.
carotenoid supplementation can influence the integrated antioxidant system.
the antioxidant system in hihi is similar to that of other species, but that the interactions between these various components are unique.
The main takeaway from our work is that
carotenoids can have a profound effect on the integrated antioxidant network of an organism.
carotenoids can have a significant impact on the antioxidant status of free living organisms.
carotenoid supplementation in hihi can lead to changes in the integrated antioxidant system, and that this may be a mechanism by which carotenoids can influence the fitness of individuals.
